thread:
Alyssa: Heads-up — ACME Mobile reporting SSE stream closes mid-response when user toggles hotspot / switches WiFi. Repro on Android 12. They see partial JSON chunks then connection tear. Escalating because customer is concerned about partial output billing.

ACME Mobile: Confirmed. Steps: open chat -> enable phone hotspot -> client shows partial chunk then 'read failed: connection reset by peer'. Happens ~2-5s after hotspot toggle.

Alyssa: Pasted a minimal server/edge snippet we captured from the session: 
```
[edge lb-23] src=10.0.1.45:52344 -> backend=10.2.8.9:443 TLS handshake ok
... streaming chunks sent ...
[edge lb-23] conn reset from client: RST, seq=0
[runtime] backend read error: EOF
[lb] nat mapping expired for 10.0.1.45:52344 after 30s idle
```

Sam: Which region/edge? any ALB/TCP proxy logs?

Alyssa: SEA edge, lb-23. Got a short tcpdump showing the client's source port vanishing right after the device toggles hotspot: 
```
14:02:11.123 IP 203.0.113.22.52344 > 34.56.78.9.443: Flags [P.], seq 123:456, ack 789
14:02:13.456 IP 203.0.113.22.52344 > 34.56.78.9.443: Flags [RST], seq 457, ack 789
// then new src ip 198.51.100.9:62000 appears a few secs later
```

Jorge: That looks like NAT rebind when hotspot toggles — client gets new IP/port and the old NAT entry gets dropped at some intermediate NAT or carrier. TCP connection is terminated (RST/FIN) -> server sees EOF. This is expected behavior for many mobile handoffs.

Jorge: Mitigations we usually recommend: keep the TCP flow alive or use application-level reconnect. Practical steps: 
- server: emit SSE heartbeat comments every ~10s so idle NAT entries stay active. Example SSE heartbeat: 
```
: ping

// or explicit event
event: ping
data: {}

```
- client: send small periodic pings or short POST heartbeats if possible, or retry/resume on short reconnect.
- infra: extend LB/proxy idle timeout and enable TCP keepalive to avoid aggressive NAT expiry.

Alyssa: Customer asked if we can detect midstream NAT rebind and return a 4xx so they don't get billed for partial output. Is that possible?

Jorge: Not really — once TCP is torn it's gone. Billing sees tokens emitted before the disconnect; we can add a flag to mark incomplete streams for manual review but that's a billing policy, not an automatic protocol signal.

Sam: Can we change LB idle from 30s to something longer for a quick trial?

DeployBot: canary change initiated — lb-23 idle_timeout: 30s -> 90s (canary) by sam via infra-runbook #3421. Rolling to 10% of traffic.

ACME Mobile: Running a quick smoke now with the canary. We'll also add a client-level ping to 10s. Will update in ~5m.

(5m later)
ACME Mobile: Quick update: with client ping + canary LB change we saw fewer midstream tears in the short run. One backgrounded app case still produced a partial chunk and then disconnect when app network suspend happened.

Jorge: For that background case we should also document that OS-level background suspension can drop sockets — recommend app uses foreground service or platform keepalive APIs where possible. We'll also add server-side default heartbeat in runtime for streaming endpoints to 10s idle.

Alyssa: I'll open a KB article with: repro steps, suggested client patch (ping every 10s), recommended LB config (idle 90s), and billing guidance for partial outputs. Marking customer ticket HIGH for follow-up.

Sam: Adding billing/ops note: flagging partial streams from this customer for manual review until client patch is rolled.

Jorge: Plan of record: (1) roll canary -> full LB config change if stable, (2) runtime default heartbeat for streaming endpoints (PR in review, ETA 24h), (3) client doc + recommended app changes.

Alyssa: Thanks team — ACME will validate and I'll update the ticket. Closing loop in ~48h unless ACME sees more flakes. :thumbsup:
